title: Sanitation and Tool-Mediated Pathogen Spread
objective: Prevent propagation tools and workflows from moving pests, pathogens, and viroids between donors and clone batches.

terms.definition: Removal of soil, debris, and organic matter from a surface before a disinfection step when required.
Use of an antimicrobial process or product to reduce or inactivate microorganisms on a surface under defined conditions.
The period a disinfectant must remain in effective contact with a surface under its label directions.
Transfer of a pest or pathogen between plants by contaminated cutting or handling tools.
Transfer of contamination from one plant, surface, batch, or workflow zone to another.
Deliberate separation of work areas and movement paths by contamination risk to limit transfer between clean and higher-risk material.

coreScience: Cutting tools contact sap and wounded tissue, creating a direct pathway between plants. Shared hands, gloves, trays, labels, water, benches, and transport containers can also move contamination.

Cleaning removes dirt and organic matter from surfaces. Disinfection uses an antimicrobial product according to its current label, including required use conditions and contact time. These are separate steps, and a quick wipe does not by itself establish disinfection.

Hop latent viroid can spread through propagation networks and mechanical practices. Containment therefore depends on donor status, workflow direction, tool control, batch segregation, testing, and traceable corrective action.
cultivationRelevance: Use a written clean-to-dirty sequence. Separate incoming, quarantine, mother, propagation, and released stock. Replace or reprocess tools and gloves according to the validated program, and stop work when contamination control is lost.

measureAndRecord.requirement: For Sanitation and Tool-Mediated Pathogen Spread, record donor or batch ID, plant or tray ID, date, operator, source position, starting condition, sanitation step, and any test or quarantine status. Preserve the original controlled note: Controlled record set: Tool ID or disposable status; cleaning/disinfection agent and lot; concentration; contact time; operator; donor and batch sequence; deviations; test and incident results.

Record rooting percentage, time to visible root or establishment, losses, abnormal growth, environmental conditions, treatment differences, and follow-up observations that would confirm or revise the interpretation.

misconceptions: One tool can safely move through a room if plants look healthy.
evidenceLimits: Agent effectiveness depends on organism, surface, soil load, concentration, time, use site, and product label. This lesson does not prescribe a universal disinfectant recipe.

knowledgeCheck: For "Sanitation and Tool-Mediated Pathogen Spread", explain the mechanism behind this objective: Prevent propagation tools and workflows from moving pests, pathogens, and viroids between donors and clone batches. Which observation or measurement would best test whether that mechanism is operating in the real crop?

A learner claims, "Alcohol instantly sterilizes every tool." Use the lesson's science and evidence limits to explain why that claim is unreliable, then name one observation or measurement that could separate the competing explanations.

Applied case — Use a written clean-to-dirty sequence. Separate incoming, quarantine, mother, propagation, and released stock. Replace or reprocess tools and gloves according to the validated program, and stop work when contamination control is lost. Build a verification plan using the lesson's record set (Controlled record set: Tool ID or disposable status; cleaning/disinfection agent and lot; concentration; contact time; operator; donor and batch sequence; deviations; test and incident results.). What would you compare before and after the action, and what result would make you revise the original interpretation?
